title: Missing ordering-safe settlement guard lets a late/non-authoritative payment_intent.canceled downgrade a settled Stripe order
description: The stripe webhook's canceled branch writes payment_status='canceled' for any order state other than already-canceled, including stripe_captured/stripe_refunded, via updatePaymentStatus which only checks the status exists in the registry. Unlike the payment_failed branch (pending-only) it has no still-pending requirement and never routes through the cancelability gate used by cancelOrder (validateStatus refuses isCancelable===false, and stripe_captured registers isCancelable:false). The write also bypasses void/refund/restock/shipment-rollup/order_canceled emission, and the changePaymentStatus hookAfter re-projects order.status to 'canceled' via 'canceled:*'. A captured order would become canceled with money captured but never refunded.
claimed_root_cause: The webhook payment-state machine lacks an ordering-safe settlement guard on the canceled transition: the handler writes 'canceled' directly via updatePaymentStatus for any non-canceled order instead of requiring a still-pending state (as the payment_failed branch does) or routing through the cancelability gate, so a late or non-authoritative canceled event can downgrade a settled order.

trace.description: stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(rawBody, sig, endpointSecret) authenticates delivery; startTransaction at line 93.

PaymentIntent from event.data.object; order resolved solely from paymentIntent.metadata.order_id via loadOrderByUuidForUpdate (149-152); amount/currency match (paymentIntentMatchesOrder) runs ONLY for isMoneyInEvent types (169-192).

case payment_intent.canceled: writes 'canceled' for any state where payment_status !== 'canceled' (305-306); contrast payment_failed requires payment_status === 'pending' (290). No refund/restock/shipment-rollup/order_canceled emission; alreadyProcessed/transaction-existence check (196-200) is ignored for this branch.

validatePaymentStatusBeforeUpdate (15-24) checks only that the status name exists in the 'oms.order.paymentStatus' registry ('canceled' registered at oms/bootstrap.ts:272-276); changePaymentStatus (26-38) is a bare UPDATE; no isCancelable gate. hookAfter('changePaymentStatus') (oms/bootstrap.ts:397-403) then re-projects order.status to 'canceled' via resolveOrderStatus('canceled', shipment) matching 'canceled:*'.

evidence.description: payment_failed branch guards with 'order.payment_status === ''pending''' - explicit settlement guard against late failures.
canceled branch guards only with 'order.payment_status !== ''canceled''' - overrides stripe_captured, stripe_authorized, stripe_refunded, paid without any settlement check.
validatePaymentStatusBeforeUpdate throws only for unregistered status; never consults isCancelable.
stripe_captured registered with isCancelable:false (22-28).

validateStatus returns false when paymentStatusConfig.isCancelable===false; cancelOrder refuses (188-190) and would emit order_canceled/restock/void - all bypassed by the webhook's direct updatePaymentStatus.
Mint is gated to payment_status='pending', limiting multi-intent reachability to the not-yet-settled window (mitigates but does not refute the late-event ordering hazard).

blockers: No sandbox and read-only target: cannot run a signed payment_intent.canceled fixture against a live/synthetic PG row to prove the downgrade end-to-end (payment_status and re-projected order.status both -> canceled, with no refund row, no order_canceled event, no restock).

Whether a genuine Stripe-delivered payment_intent.canceled can reach an already-settled order depends on Stripe's event-delivery ordering/retry semantics (a single intent that reached succeeded cannot later be canceled per Stripe's model, so the downgrade requires delayed/redelivered cancellation of an earlier state or a race on an authorized-but-capturing intent) - an external runtime fact not decidable from source.

validation_plan.local: Bounded fixture plan: unit/integration test harness - create order rows at stripe_captured/stripe_authorized/stripe_refunded and a pending row; call the webhook route with a constructEvent-signed payload (stripe.webhooks.generateTestHeaderString against a test endpoint secret) of type payment_intent.canceled; assert non-pending orders flip payment_status/order.status to canceled while payment_failed does not, and that no payment_transaction/refund/order_canceled event is created; also assert (refutation check) that createPaymentIntent on a stripe_captured order returns 'Invalid order', bounding the multi-intent attack surface to the pending window.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed plan: on a test Stripe account, place an order, auto-capture to stripe_captured, then deliberately redeliver/retry a pre-existing payment_intent.canceled event (or pause+resume webhook delivery to force late delivery of a cancellation that raced a manual capture) and observe whether the order row is downgraded to canceled without a refund/restock; monitor reset of order.status via the 'canceled:*' projection.
